stem: Which kingdom contains organisms whose bodies are made of thread-like hyphae with cell walls of chitin?

options.rationale: Hyphae and chitin cell walls are diagnostic features of fungi.
Plant cell walls are made of cellulose, and plants are not made of hyphae.
Prokaryotes are single cells with no nucleus.
Animal cells have no cell walls.

explanation: Most fungi are made of a network (mycelium) of thread-like hyphae, and their cell walls contain chitin. Plants have cellulose walls and animals have no walls at all.

stem: An organism is a single cell. It has a cell wall and ribosomes, and its DNA is a circular loop in the cytoplasm. It has no nucleus. Which kingdom does it belong to?

options.rationale: No nucleus and a circular loop of DNA are the diagnostic features of prokaryotes.
Protoctists have a nucleus.
Fungal cells have a nucleus.
Plants are multicellular and their cells have a nucleus.

explanation: Having no nucleus is the key feature: the organism is a prokaryote, such as a bacterium. Its DNA is a circular chromosome lying free in the cytoplasm.

stem: Which feature do plant cells have that fungal cells do **not**?

options.rationale: Fungal cells also have walls, made of chitin.
Fungal cells also have a nucleus.
All cells have cytoplasm.
Fungi have no chlorophyll and cannot photosynthesise.

explanation: Both plant and fungal cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm and a cell wall (cellulose in plants, chitin in fungi). Only plant cells have chloroplasts with chlorophyll, so only plants photosynthesise.

stem: Which of these organisms is a protoctist?

options.rationale: Yeast is a single-celled fungus.
*Plasmodium* is a single-celled organism with a nucleus: a protoctist.
Bacteria are prokaryotes.
HIV is a virus and does not belong to any kingdom.

explanation: *Plasmodium* is a single-celled organism with a nucleus that lives as a parasite, so it is a protoctist. Yeast is a fungus, bacteria are prokaryotes and viruses are not placed in any kingdom.

stem: Match each organism with the kingdom it belongs to.
explanation: *Mucor* is a fungus (hyphae, chitin walls), *Amoeba* a protoctist (single cell with a nucleus), *Lactobacillus* a prokaryote (no nucleus), the msasa a plant and the tigerfish an animal. 'Not placed in any kingdom' describes viruses.

stem: (Supplement) True or false: viruses are made of cells that are much smaller than bacterial cells.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not true. Viruses are much smaller than bacteria, but they are not cells at all: just genetic material in a protein coat.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct. A virus is not a cell; it is genetic material (DNA or RNA) inside a protein coat.

explanation: Viruses have no cytoplasm, cell membrane or ribosomes. Each particle is only genetic material inside a protein coat, and it can reproduce only inside a living host cell.

stem: True or false: animal cells have no cell walls.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct. Animal cells are surrounded only by a cell membrane.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true: animal cells have a cell membrane but no cell wall.

explanation: Animal cells have a cell membrane but no cell wall. Plants (cellulose), fungi (chitin) and prokaryotes all have cell walls.

stem: Name the substance that makes up the cell walls of fungi.

rejected.feedback: Cellulose is found in plant cell walls; fungal walls are made of chitin.
Glycogen is the carbohydrate that fungi store, not their wall material.

explanation: Fungal cell walls are made of chitin, which is different from the cellulose of plant cell walls.

stem: Name the type of nutrition in which a fungus feeds on dead organic matter by releasing enzymes onto it and absorbing the soluble products.

rejected.feedback: Parasites feed on living hosts; feeding on dead matter is saprotrophic.
Holozoic nutrition means taking food into the body and digesting it inside, as animals do.
Autotrophs make their own food, for example by photosynthesis.

explanation: Saprotrophic nutrition: the fungus secretes digestive enzymes onto dead organic matter (such as bread or fallen leaves) and absorbs the small, soluble molecules produced.

stem: A microscopic organism from the green water of a cattle trough is a single cell with a nucleus and chloroplasts. It has no cell wall and swims using a flagellum. Which kingdom does it belong to, and why?

options.rationale: Plants are multicellular and their cells have cellulose walls; a single cell with a nucleus is a protoctist.

options.content: Prokaryotes, because it is a single cell
options.rationale: Prokaryotes have no nucleus.

options.content: Protoctists, because it is a single cell with a nucleus
options.rationale: Single-celled organisms with a nucleus are protoctists, whether they photosynthesise like plants or move like animals.

options.content: Animals, because it has no cell wall and can swim
options.rationale: Animals are multicellular, and animal cells have no chloroplasts.

explanation: The organism has a nucleus (so it is not a prokaryote) and it is a single cell (so it is neither a plant nor an animal). It photosynthesises like a plant but swims like an animal: it is a protoctist, such as *Euglena*.
hints: Use the nucleus first, then the number of cells.

stem: (Supplement) A plant has long, narrow leaves with parallel veins, and its flowers have six petals. Which group does it belong to?

options.rationale: Ferns do not produce flowers.
Parallel veins and flower parts in threes or multiples of three.
Dicotyledons have branching veins and flower parts in fours or fives.
Protoctists are mostly single-celled and have no flowers.

explanation: Parallel leaf veins and flower parts in multiples of three (six petals) are features of monocotyledons, such as lilies and onions.
hints: Look at the leaf veins, then count the petals: threes or fives?

stem: (Supplement) Select **all** the structures that a virus particle has.

options.rationale: Every virus has a protein coat.
The genetic material carries the instructions for making new viruses.
Viruses have no cytoplasm.
Viruses are not cells and have no cell membrane.
Viruses use the host cell's ribosomes.
Viruses have no nucleus.

explanation: A virus particle consists only of genetic material (DNA or RNA) inside a protein coat. It has none of the structures of a cell, which is why it can reproduce only inside a host cell.
hints: A virus has only two main parts.

stem: Complete the sentences about two of the five kingdoms.

payload.template: Single-celled organisms with no nucleus belong to the kingdom of {{blank:a}}. Organisms that are mostly single-celled but have a nucleus, such as *Amoeba*, belong to the kingdom of {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Prokaryotes (Prokaryotae or Monera), such as bacteria, have no nucleus. Protoctists (Protoctista or Protista), such as *Amoeba* and *Plasmodium*, have a nucleus and are mostly single-celled.

stem: (Supplement) Which statement describes ferns?

options.content: They have roots, stems and leaves (fronds), and reproduce by spores made on the underside of the fronds.
options.rationale: Ferns have no flowers or seeds.

options.content: They reproduce by seeds produced inside fruits.
options.rationale: That describes flowering plants.

options.content: They are made of hyphae and feed on dead material.
options.rationale: That describes fungi.

options.content: They are single cells with chloroplasts.
options.rationale: That describes some protoctists.

explanation: Ferns are plants with roots, stems and leaves called fronds. They have no flowers or seeds; they reproduce by spores formed in clusters on the underside of the fronds.
hints: Do ferns produce flowers and seeds?

stem:
The table describes four organisms, A to D.

| Organism | Number of cells | Nucleus | Cell wall | Chlorophyll |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | One | Absent | Present (not cellulose) | Absent |
| B | Many | Present | Absent | Absent |
| C | One | Present | Present (chitin) | Absent |
| D | Many | Present | Present (cellulose) | Present |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each organism with its kingdom.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Organism C is single-celled. Explain why it is classified as a fungus and not as a prokaryote or a plant.

points.description: It has a nucleus, so it is not a prokaryote
Its wall is made of chitin / it has no chlorophyll, so it is not a plant (it is a single-celled fungus such as yeast)

parts.explanation: Organism C has a nucleus, so it cannot be a prokaryote. Its cell wall is made of chitin and it has no chlorophyll, which are features of fungi, not plants. It is a single-celled fungus, like yeast.

explanation: A has no nucleus: a prokaryote. B is multicellular with no walls or chlorophyll: an animal. C has a nucleus and chitin walls: a fungus (like yeast). D is multicellular with cellulose walls and chlorophyll: a plant.
hints: Check for a nucleus first; then look at the cell wall material and chlorophyll.

stem: (Supplement) Explain why viruses are not placed in any of the five kingdoms. [3]

points.description: Viruses are not made of cells / have no cytoplasm, cell membrane or ribosomes
They consist only of genetic material (DNA or RNA) in a protein coat
They can only reproduce inside living host cells / show no characteristics of life (respiration, nutrition, growth, excretion) outside a host

answerSpec.modelAnswer: All five kingdoms are made up of organisms with cells. Viruses are not cells: each particle is only genetic material (DNA or RNA) inside a protein coat, with no cytoplasm, membrane or ribosomes. Outside a host cell a virus does not respire, feed, grow or excrete, and it can reproduce only by using the materials and enzymes inside a living host cell. So viruses do not fit into any kingdom.

explanation: The kingdoms classify cellular organisms. A virus has no cell structure and shows the characteristics of life only by reproducing inside host cells.
hints: Which characteristics of life can a virus show on its own?

stem: Yeast is a single-celled organism. Why is it classified as a fungus rather than as a bacterium?

options.rationale: Bacteria are single-celled too.
Many bacteria can also respire anaerobically.

options.content: Its cell has a nucleus and a wall made of chitin.
options.rationale: A nucleus rules out prokaryotes; chitin walls are a fungal feature.

options.content: It is used to make bread.
options.rationale: Uses do not decide the kingdom; bacteria are used to make yoghurt.

explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes with no nucleus. Yeast cells have a nucleus and chitin cell walls, the features of fungi.
hints: Which structure is missing from every bacterial cell?

stem: Which feature is found in plants but **not** in animals?

options.rationale: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus.
Plants photosynthesise; animals cannot.
Both have a cell membrane.
Both plants and animals are multicellular.

explanation: Plants have chloroplasts with chlorophyll and cellulose cell walls; animals have neither. Both kingdoms are multicellular with cells that have a nucleus and a membrane.

stem: (Supplement) A groundnut seed splits into two halves (seed leaves). The plant's leaves have a network of branching veins, and its flowers have five petals. Which group does the groundnut plant belong to?

options.rationale: Monocotyledons have one cotyledon, parallel veins and flower parts in threes.
Ferns have no flowers or seeds.
Groundnuts are multicellular plants.
Two cotyledons, branching veins and flower parts in fives.

explanation: Two cotyledons, net-veined leaves and flower parts in fives are all features of dicotyledons. Beans and groundnuts are typical dicotyledons; maize is a monocotyledon.
hints: How many seed leaves does the groundnut seed have?

stem:
A biologist finds a new microorganism in mud from the edge of Lake Kariba. Its features are:

- a single cell about 40 μm long
- a nucleus and mitochondria
- no cell wall and no chloroplasts
- it moves with a long flagellum and takes in bacteria as food

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which kingdom should it be placed in?

options.rationale: Animals are multicellular.
It has a nucleus and mitochondria.
Fungi have cell walls and absorb food rather than taking in whole bacteria.
It is a single cell with a nucleus.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give **two** features from the list that rule out the prokaryote kingdom.

points.description: It has mitochondria / it is much larger (about 40 μm) than a typical bacterium

parts.explanation: It has a nucleus, which prokaryotes lack, and it has mitochondria (prokaryotes have none). It is also about 40 μm long, far larger than a typical bacterium.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The organism feeds like an animal. Explain why it is still not placed in the animal kingdom.

points.description: Animals are multicellular, so single-celled organisms with a nucleus are protoctists

parts.explanation: Animals are multicellular. This organism is a single cell with a nucleus, so even though it takes in food like an animal it is an animal-like protoctist.

explanation: The organism has a nucleus (not a prokaryote), no wall or chlorophyll (not a plant or fungus) and is single-celled (not an animal), so it is an animal-like protoctist.
hints: Work through the features in order: nucleus, number of cells, cell wall, nutrition.

stem: True or false: fungi store carbohydrate as starch, as plants do.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not true. Fungi store carbohydrate as glycogen, like animals; plants store starch.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct. Fungi store glycogen, not starch.

explanation: Plants store carbohydrate as starch, but fungi store it as glycogen. This is one reason fungi are not classified as plants.
hints: Which storage carbohydrate do animals and fungi share?

stem: *Plasmodium* is a single-celled parasite with a nucleus. It causes malaria. Name the kingdom it belongs to.

rejected.feedback: *Plasmodium* has a nucleus, so it is not a prokaryote.
Animals are multicellular; *Plasmodium* is a single cell.
*Plasmodium* has a nucleus, so it is not a bacterium.

explanation: *Plasmodium* is a single cell with a nucleus, so it belongs to the protoctists (Protoctista or Protista). It is spread by female *Anopheles* mosquitoes.
